This document will go over the high level UI specifications for the web 
validation tool. These specifications are not meant to specify the **visual**
aspects of the tool (i.e. they are not meant to be pretty) but are more meant
to specify functional aspects of the UI.

The specifications will go through each feature outlined in the high level
specifications and explain their functional aspects by using wireframe 
diagrams as well as flow diagrams.

# Screen Types

The different screens that are part of the UI can be broadly classified into 
two categories:

1. **Primary Screens**: These screens consist of two panels, a sidebar and an 
   information panel. The sidebar has screen specific actions that the user can 
   do. The information panel mainly consists of text.
2. **Dialog Screens**: These screens are used when a process cannot be completed 
   in a single step (for e.g., [uploading a dataset](#dataset-upload), or for 
   actions that require confirmation from a user. They are overlaid on top of a 
   primary screen, and a user is not allowed to interact with the primary screen 
   until the dialog is closed.

# Features 

Each of the next sub-sections will go over the features for the tool and the 
user flows and/or wireframes for them. The sections that show flow diagrams
will not go through each screen in the flow, those can be seen in the 
[screens](#screens) section.

## [Dataset Upload](../spec.qmd#dataset-upload)

There are multiple screens from which a user can start the process of uploading 
a dataset, this section will focus on the home screen as the starting point.
The image below contains the flow diagram for uploading a dataset from the home
screen.

![upload dataset from the home screen](../../dist/upload-dataset-from-home-screen.png)

The user can initiate the upload dataset flow by clicking on the **Upload 
Dataset** button from any screen where its available.

In addition, the user should not be allowed to proceed from the **Configure 
Dataset** screens unless all the dataset metadata is valid.

This flow can also be initiated from the [Validation Summary](#from-the-validation-summary-screen) 
screen and [View Dataset](#from-the-view-dataset-screen) screen. The flows are 
identical to the one above, with the only difference being the start screen.

## [Dataset Metadata](../spec.qmd#dataset-metadata)

* From the [view dataset screen](#view-dataset-screen) whose flow is shown below

![configure dataset from view dataset screen](../../dist/configure-dataset.png)

## [Upload Report](../spec.qmd#upload-report)

The user can view the upload report from the [View Dataset](#view-dataset-screen)
screen. The two ways the user can access this screen is by:

1. Successfully uploading a new dataset which takes them to the screen; and
2. Clicking on an already uploaded dataset which can be done from the 
   [Validation Summary Screen](#validation-summary-screen) or the 
   [View Dataset Screen](#view-dataset-screen)

# Screens

The next sub-sections will go over the different screens presented in the flow
diagrams above.

## Home Screen

![home screen](../../dist/home-screen.png)

The home screen is shown to the user when they land on the open the tool. From 
the home screen they can:

* **Upload a dataset**: Using the **Upload Dataset** button
* **View their validation profiles**: Using the **View Validation Profiles** 
  button. 
* **View Tutorials**: Using the **Tutorial** button

## Choose Dataset Dialog 

![choose dataset dialog](../../dist/choose-dataset-dialog.png)

This screen is part of the [upload dataset flow](#dataset-upload-and-dataset-metadata)
where the user can choose a CSV or Excel file they want uploaded to the tool.

The tool should use the [file chooser dialog](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/file)
that ships with every browser. The tool should also prevent the user from 
choosing files that aren't CSV or Excel files.

The **Close** button allows the user to cancel the dataset upload process, 
taking them back to the screen from where they started the flow.

## Configure Dataset Dialog 

Depending on the dataset that the user wants to configure, a different 
screen is shown.

### Configure CSV Dataset Dialog 

![Configure CSV dataset dialog](../../dist/configure-csv-dataset-dialog.png)

On this screen the user can:

* Select the ODM version that this dataset is for. This is the **ODM version**
  dropdown. Refer to the high level specifications for what versions the tool
  supports.
* Select the ODM table that this dataset represents. This is done using the 
  **Table** dropdown.
* Save the configuration by clicking the **Save** button. 
* Cancel the configuration by clicking the **Close** button.

In addition,

* The **\<CSV file name\>** text should be replaced with the file name of the 
  dataset.
* The user should be allowed to save the configuration only if the ODM version 
  and table dropdown have been correctly filled in.

### Configure Excel Dataset Dialog 

![configure excel dataset dialog](../../dist/configure-excel-dataset-dialog.png)

From this screen the user can:

* Choose the ODM version the dataset is for. This is done using the **ODM 
  version** dropdown. For the list of supported ODM versions, look at the high 
  level specifications.
* Choose the ODM table that each sheet maps to. This is done using the dropdowns
  at the bottom of the **Tables** text.
* Save the configuration by clicking the **Save** button. 
* Cancel the configuration by clicking the **Close** button.

In addition,

* The **\<Excel file name\>** text should be replaced with the file name of the 
  dataset
* The user should be allowed to save the configuration only if the ODM version 
  and table dropdowns have been correctly filled in.

## View Dataset Screen

![view dataset screen](../../dist/view-dataset-screen.png)

This screen is shown when the user uploads a new dataset or selects a dataset
on another screen. It allows the user to view summary details about the 
uploaded dataset.

From this screen the user can:

* Select another dataset from the **Choose Dataset** panel.
* Upload a new dataset using the **Upload Dataset** button
* View their validation profiles using the **View Validation Profiles** button
* Re-configure their dataset by clicking the **Configure Dataset** button
* View the **Upload Report** which summarizes the uploaded dataset.
* Navigate to the [Validation Summary](#validation-summary-screen) by clicking 
  on one of them in the **Previous Validations** panel.
* Start a new validation using the **Validate Dataset** button
* View the tutorials using the **Tutorial** button.

## Validation Summary Screen

![validation summary screen](../../dist/validation-summary-screen.png)

This screen provides summary for a particular dataset validation. From this
screen the user can:

* Navigate to the [View Dataset](#view-dataset-screen) by clicking on one of
  them in the **Choose Dataset** panel.
* Upload a new dataset by clicking on the **Upload Dataset** button
* View their validation profiles by clicking on the **View Validation Profiles**
  button
* Navigate to the summary for another validation by clicking on one of them
  in the **Previous Validations** panel.
* Start a new validation by clicking the **Validate Dataset** button
* View the tutorials by clicking the **Tutorials** button
* View the upload report for the selected validation
* View the entire validation report by clicking the **Validation Report** button

## New Validation Dialog 

![new validation dialog](../../dist/new-validation-dialog.png)

This screen is used by the user to start a new validation and is part of the
[validate dataset](#dataset-validation) flow.

From this screen the user can:

* Choose the validation profile they want to use using the **validation 
  profile** dropdown
* View the properties of their selected profile using the **Validation
  Properties** panel
* Customize the validation by creating a new profile. This is done by clicking
  the **Customize Validation** button
* Start the validation by clicking the **Start Validation** button
* Cancel the new validation by clicking the **Cancel** button

In addition,

* By default the selected validation profile should be one created by the
  ODM staff

## Validating Dialog 

![validating dialog](../../dist/validating-dialog.png)

This screen is part of the [validate dataset](#dataset-validation) flow.

From this screen the user can:

* View their validation progress
* Cancel the validation by pressing the **Cancel** button

## Cancel Validation Dialog 

![cancel validation dialog](../../dist/cancel-validation-dialog.png)

This screen is part of the [validate dataset](#dataset-validation) flow. Its 
used to confirm with the user if they want to cancel their validation.

From this screen the user can:

* Cancel the validation process by clicking the **Yes** button
* Continue the validation process by clicking the **Not** button

## View Validation Profiles Dialog

![view validation profiles dialog](../../dist/view-validation-profiles-dialog.png)

From this screen the user can:

* View the different validation profiles they have
* Edit any one by clicking the **Edit** button
* Download any one by clicking the **Download** button
* Delete any one by clocking the **Delete** button
* Create a new profile by clicking the **Create New Profile** button
* Return to the previous screen by clicking the **Close** button

## Create Validation Profile Dialog 

![create validation profile dialog](../../dist/create-validation-profile-dialog.png)

From this screen the user can:

* Edit the name of their new validation profile. This field is mandatory.
* Edit the description of their new validation profile. This field is optional.
* Edit the rules they want to be part of this profile. At least one rule should
  be selected.
* Create the new profile by clicking the **Create Profile** button. The above
  validations need to pass for the profile creation.
* Create a new profile by uploading a validation profile. When they upload the
  file, the tool should attempt to fill in the fields using the information in
  the file. This is done using the **Upload Profile** button.
* Cancel the creation with the **Cancel** button.

## Edit Validation Profile Dialog 

![edit validation profile dialog](../../dist/edit-validation-profile-dialog.png)

This screen has the same functionality as the [Create Validation Profile](#create-validation-profile-screen)
screen.

## Delete Validation Profile Dialog 

![delete validation profile dialog](../../dist/delete-validation-profile-dialog.png)

Used to confirm if the user wants to delete a validation profile. From this 
screen the user can:

* Confirm they want to delete a validation profile by clicking the **Yes** 
  button
* Stop the deletion by clicking the **No** button

## Choose Validation Profile Dialog 

![choose validation profile screen](../../dist/choose-validation-profile-dialog.png)

When uploading a validation profile, this screen allows the user to choose a 
validation profile file from their computer. It should use the [File 
Dialog](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/file)
provided by the browser.

## Validation Report Dialog 

![view validation report dialog](../../dist/validation-report-dialog.png)

From this screen the user can:

* View the full results of a validation
* Download the validation report by clicking on one of the options in the
  **Download Report** dropdown.
* Set what they want to include in the downloaded report by using the **Download
  Options** dropdown.
* Close the validation report by clicking the **Close** button
